detail.body:
# PR type

- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Document Updates
- [ ] More Models or Datasets Support

# PR information

Related issue: none.

SFT accuracy currently copies predictions and labels to the CPU and builds Python correctness lists on every micro-batch, even when `logging_steps` is large. Accumulate device-side correct/valid counts instead, and transfer the reduced counters when metrics are logged. This preserves token weighting across variable-length batches and excludes sequences with no supervised labels.

Use one tensor implementation for accuracy, with the existing list return format as the default. Packed sequence accuracy uses prefix sums to avoid reading individual GPU boundaries in Python. Add a small `MeanMetric.update_counts()` entry point so counters bypass the scalar `.item()` in `update()`. Sequence-parallel prediction/label gathering is unchanged.

Production changes total +46/-35 lines. The existing sequence-parallel test double is adapted to accept counts; no new test cases or benchmark files are included.

AI assistance: implementation, local validation, and this description were prepared with OpenAI Codex. Human review checklist items remain unchecked in this draft.

## Experiment results

On an RTX A1000 Laptop GPU with PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130, BF16 logits and vocabulary size 32,000, the actual accuracy hook was measured including argmax and a logging flush every 100 micro-batches. Timings are medians of three warmed-up runs against main at `80e55df90`.

| Accuracy / input | Before | After | D2H copies over 3 micro-batches, excluding logging |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Token, batch 1, length 8,192 | 3.116 ms | 3.084 ms | 6 → 0 |
| Sequence, batch 1, length 8,192, 64 packed sequences | 5.425 ms | 3.114 ms | 1,158 → 0 |

These are accuracy-hook timings, not end-to-end training speedups. Accuracy values matched exactly. A small native GPT-2 through `Seq2SeqTrainer.compute_loss` also produced identical loss, parameter gradients, and accuracy logs for token/sequence accuracy with logging intervals of 1 and 100.

Validation:

- `uvx pre-commit run --all-files` — passed.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_acc_metrics.py tests/sequence_parallel/test_seq_accuracy.py tests/utils/test_reranker_metrics.py ../ms-swift-sft-accuracy-audit/removed_test_acc_metrics.py` — 28 passed: 14 existing repository cases and 14 local checks kept outside the patch. The local checks compare against the original implementation and reject `.cpu()`, `.numpy()`, `.item()`, and `.tolist()` calls during accuracy accumulation.
- `python ../ms-swift-sft-accuracy-audit/benchmark_accuracy.py` and `python ../ms-swift-sft-accuracy-audit/validate_sft_loss.py` — local profiler and training comparisons described above; these scripts are outside the repository.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

# Checklist

- [x] I have linked the related issue above, if there is one.
- [ ] I have reviewed and understand every changed line, and I can explain how the change works and why it is correct.
- [x] I have run the relevant tests or reproductions locally, and included the commands and results above (if applicable).
- [ ] I am responsible for the content of this PR, regardless of how it was produced.

+    """Return per-item correctness, or device-side [correct, valid] counts for accumulation."""
+    preds, labels = torch.as_tensor(preds), torch.as_tensor(labels)
     if preds.ndim >= 2 and not is_encoder_decoder:
         labels = labels[..., 1:]
         preds = preds[..., :-1]
-    if np.issubdtype(labels.dtype, np.floating) or preds.shape != labels.shape:
+    if torch.is_floating_point(labels) or preds.shape != labels.shape:
         return {}
 
     masks = labels != -100
-    if acc_strategy == 'token' or preds.ndim == 1:  # 'single_label_classification'
-        acc_list = (preds[masks] == labels[masks]).tolist()
-    else:
-        acc_list = []
+    correct = preds == labels
+    if acc_strategy != 'token' and preds.ndim >= 2:
         if cu_seqlens is not None and masks.shape[0] == 1:
-            # padding_free
-            for i in range(cu_seqlens.shape[0] - 1):
-                start, end = cu_seqlens[i], cu_seqlens[i + 1]
-                mask = masks[0, start:end]
-                # np.all() of an empty selection is True, so a sequence without any supervised label
-                # would be scored as a correct prediction.
-                if not mask.any():
-                    continue
-                acc_list.append(np.all(preds[0, start:end][mask] == labels[0, start:end][mask]))
+            # Prefix sums match packed slices without reading GPU boundaries in Python.
+            bounds = torch.as_tensor(cu_seqlens, device=preds.device, dtype=torch.long)
+            bounds = torch.where(bounds < 0, bounds + masks.shape[-1], bounds).clamp(0, masks.shape[-1])
+            counts = torch.stack([masks[0], masks[0] & ~correct[0]]).cumsum(dim=-1)
+            counts = torch.cat([counts.new_zeros((2, 1)), counts], dim=-1)
+            counts = counts[:, bounds[1:]] - counts[:, bounds[:-1]]
+            masks = counts[0] > 0
+            correct = counts[1] == 0
         else:
-            for i, m in enumerate(masks):
-                if not m.any():
-                    continue
-                acc_list.append(np.all(preds[i, m] == labels[i, m]))
-    if not acc_list:
-        return {}
+            correct = (correct | ~masks).flatten(1).all(dim=-1)
+            masks = masks.flatten(1).any(dim=-1)
+    if return_counts:
+        acc_list = torch.stack([(correct & masks).sum(), masks.sum()])
+    else:
+        acc_list = correct[masks].tolist()
+        if not acc_list:
+            return {}
     return {f'{acc_strategy}_acc' if preds.ndim >= 2 else 'acc': acc_list}

     def compute(self):

             dist.all_reduce(tensor, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM, group=self.group)
-            self.state, self.count = tensor[0].item(), int(tensor[1].item())
